why: The tracker's on-disk layout has two readers since tick kya: internal/tick's
Store (Go, which owns the format and writes every record) and
cloud/factory/src/tick-membership.ts (the control plane, which reads one
record at a commit through GitHub's contents API to prove a requested wave's
ticks belong to the run's epic). This file is what both suites pin themselves
to, the same way worker-boot-contract.json pins the three readers of the
It matters more here than a parity fixture usually does, because of which way
the Worker's check fails: a tracker it cannot read ALLOWS the wave. So a
layout change landing in Go alone would not break the factory loudly — it
would silently turn every membership verdict into 'unreadable' and the check
would stop refusing anything, with both suites still green. This fixture is
what makes that change fail a test instead.
